name: IVOZ Provider
what_it_is: IvozProvider is a multitenant VoIP telephony provider platform built on Kamailio 5.7 (SIP proxy/media relay) and Asterisk 20 LTS (PBX/application server), designed for horizontal scaling and load balancing. It provides a full-stack solution with multi-level web portals (platform, brand, company, user) and a REST API backed by Percona/MariaDB and Redis.
components: Asterisk 20 LTS with PJSIP channel driver (PBX / application server)
Web portals: platform, brand, client/company, user (Node.js / ivoz-ui)
measurement: Health checks on all Docker services (MySQL ping, Redis CLI ping, HTTP curl)
No built-in metrics export or monitoring stack observed in docker-compose
configuration: Multi-level admin hierarchy: platform admin > brand admin > company admin > end user
XDEBUG toggle via build arg (XDEBUG=true/false) in backend service
BACKEND_URL environment variable configures portal-to-backend routing
MariaDB credentials and database name set via environment variables (MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD, MYSQL_DATABASE, MYSQL_USER, MYSQL_PASSWORD)
UID/GID binding for backend and portal containers
Node environment selectable via NODE_ENV (default: development)
Static internal subnet 10.189.4.0/24 with fixed IPs per service
modes: Distributed installation (components spread across multiple machines)
Standalone installation (all components on a single machine)
constraints: No explicit port mappings defined in docker-compose — external access requires additional network configuration
No resource limits (CPU/memory) specified for any Docker service
No restart policies configured — containers will not auto-recover from crashes in default compose setup
Credentials hardcoded as environment variables in docker-compose (development-only pattern; not suitable for production as-is)
Backend health check has a 120-second startup delay — slow to become ready in automated pipelines
docker_services: backend (PHP REST API + FastAGI, IP 10.189.4.20, depends on data+redis)
portal-platform (Node.js UI, IP 10.189.4.30, depends on backend)
portal-brand (Node.js UI, IP 10.189.4.31, depends on backend)
portal-client (Node.js UI, IP 10.189.4.32, depends on backend)
portal-user (Node.js UI, IP 10.189.4.33, depends on backend)
notable_absences: No fault injection or chaos engineering tooling
No SIP load-testing or traffic-generation service in compose
No TLS/SRTP configuration visible in compose (may be handled at Kamailio level outside compose)
No Kamailio or Asterisk service defined in docker-compose (compose targets development/portal only, not the full telephony stack)
